title: The ethical drinker: Putting people first is key to making great wines
content: <p>Natalie is Decanter's France editor, commissioning and writing content on French wines (excluding Bordeaux) across print and digital. She writes Decanter's coverage of Languedoc wines, as well as a monthly magazine column, The Ethical Drinker, which unpicks the thorny topic of sustainability in wine. </p><p>It was during her time studying for a French and Italian degree that Natalie began her foray into wine: tutoring French in exchange for WSET lessons in her spare time (she now realises who got the better deal!). She moved to the Languedoc after graduating to work for a vineyard tour company, before returning to the UK in 2016 to join the tastings team at Decanter.</p><p>She worked across Decanter's panel tastings and wine competitions before becoming awards competition manager, overseeing the competitive and judging elements of the Decanter World Wine Awards, Decanter Asia Wine Awards and Retailer Awards, and completing her WSET Diploma in 2019.</p><p>In 2021 she made the shift to the Decanter editorial team, and is now the Regional Editor for France (outside of Bordeaux and Burgundy).</p><p>She will always be drawn to the wines of the Languedoc and Roussillon, but her wine tastes are wide-ranging and she can't resist a glass of Manzanilla Sherry or the lure of an obscure grape variety.</p>

title: Spirits briefing: The Cocktail Hour review and how to make a Negroni Seltz
content: <div class="author-description"><p class="p1"><span class="s1">Julie Sheppard joined the Decanter team in 2018 and is Regional Editor for Australia, New Zealand and South Africa &amp; Spirits Editor. </span></p><p class="p1"><span class="s1">Before Decanter, she worked for a range of drinks and food titles, including as managing editor of both <em>Imbibe</em> and <em>Square Meal</em>, associate publisher of </span><em>The Drinks Business</em><span class="s1">, senior editor of the Octopus Publishing Group and Supplements editor of <em>Harpers Wine &amp; Spirit</em>. As a contributor, she has over 20 years’ experience writing <span class="Apple-converted-space">about food, drink and travel </span>for a wide range of publications, including <em><span class="Apple-converted-space">Condé Nast Traveller, </span></em></span><span class="s1"><em>Delicious</em>, <em>Waitrose Kitchen</em>, <em>Waitrose Drinks</em>, <em>Time Out</em> and national newspapers including <em>The Telegraph</em> and <em>The Sunday Times</em>.</span></p><p class="p1"><span class="s1">.</span></p></div>

title: Washington wine quiz: Can you get a Super(Sonic) score?
content: <p>A longtime U.S. wine writer, New Jersey–based Dana Nigro joined <em>Decanter</em> in June 2026. Previously, she spent more than 25 years with <em>Wine Spectator </em>in New York City, where she started as news editor, then became a senior editor for the magazine and the digital managing editor—responsible for the website, social media and apps.</p><p>She fell in love with wine while studying magazine journalism in New York’s Finger Lakes wine region, where she took advantage of the excellent wine program at Cornell University’s School of Hotel Administration. As a result, one of her passions is Riesling. Another is sustainability in wine—from the vineyard soil to the winery buildings to the bottles (and boxes). </p><p>While reporting on U.S. wine, Nigro covered topics such as the battle to legalize direct shipping up through the U.S. Supreme Court decision in <em>Granholm v. Heald</em>, the rise of women in California’s wine industry, and the evolution of West Coast winegrowing from its early sustainability certifications to its movement toward regenerative farming.</p><p>Before her wine career, she worked at a fine-dining restaurant, served as a reporter covering local news and the international travel industry, and taught scuba diving.</p>

title: Cocktails, food and harvest: Five unexpected ways to enjoy Port on Port Wine Day
summary: Forget about your warm glass of Tawny and beige cheese platter. There are fun, refreshing ways to enjoy the different styles of Port. From the simplicity of a Port & Tonic to unexpected food pairings, there's something for everyone and every mood.
content: <div class="author-description"><p><span style="font-weight: 400">Ines is Decanter’s regional editor for Spain, Portugal and South America. Born and raised in Lisbon, Portugal, she grew up chasing her grandfather among his vines in Ribatejo and thus her love for all things wine began. After completing her Masters Degree in Architecture, Ines worked as a project manager while writing about wine and doing cellar consulting on the side. After moving to London in 2015, she decided to dedicate herself fully to the wine industry and joined the sommelier team at Michelin-starred Spring, Somerset House. Stints at Noble Rot and The Laughing Heart followed, while completing her WSET Diploma in Wines and Spirits. Her work as a judge and writer eventually became her full time commitment and she joined Decanter in 2019 as wine database editor. </span></p></div>

title: Confessions of an insider: Why we all crave Riesling and Negronis
summary: What links Riesling and Negroni –two drinks that, on the face of it, couldn't be further apart?
content: <div class="author-description"><p>James Button is Decanter’s regional editor for Italy, responsible for all of Decanter's Italian content in print and online.</p><p>Like many others, he started his wine career at Majestic Wine, giving him a strong grounding in the subject before successfully completing the WSET Level 4 Diploma in 2010. From 2014 to 2016 he managed the fine wine department of a startup wine company in London, before joining Decanter as digital sub-editor.</p><p>Outside of wine, James enjoys cooking, skiing, playing guitar and cycling.</p></div>

title: Cult Spanish wine from century-old vines: Numanthia winemaker Jesús Jiménez on Toro's special heritage
summary: 'You'll be surprised when you taste Numanthia'...
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Chris Mercer is a Bristol-based freelance editor and journalist who spent nearly four years as digital editor of <strong>Decanter.com</strong>, having previously been <em>Decanter’s</em> news editor across online and print.</p><p>He has written about, and reported on, the wine and food sectors for more than 10 years for both consumer and trade media.</p><p>Chris first became interested in the wine world while living in Languedoc-Roussillon after completing a journalism Masters in the UK. These days, his love of wine commonly tests his budgeting skills.</p><p>Beyond wine, Chris also has an MSc in food policy and has a particular interest in sustainability issues. He has also been a food judge at the UK’s Great Taste Awards.</p></div>

title: Under 30s Wine Trade Sips: Tom, 24
summary: To help spread the word that wine is for everyone, we ask Zoomers working in the wine industry – bars, restaurants, cellars and retail – to share their experience of a bottle they love.
content: <p>Tom Heading is an Australian completing a Masters in Oenology and Viticulture in Montpellier, France.</p>

title: 'Visiting Château Rayas made me realise there are four stages of wine appreciation'
content: <p>Matt Walls is an award-winning freelance wine writer and consultant, contributing regular articles to various print and online titles including Decanter, where he is a contributing editor. He has particular interest in the Rhône Valley; he is chair of the Rhône panel at the Decanter World Wine Awards and is the owner of travel and events company www.rhoneroots.com. </p><p>He writes about all areas of wine, but specialises in the Rhône.</p><p>Matt&#39;s latest book, The Smart Traveller&#39;s Wine Guide to the Rhône Valley, was published in September 2025.</p>

title: Margaret River Vintage Report: 2024 Chardonnay and 2023 Cabernet Sauvignon
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Cassandra Charlick is a Margaret River-based wine and travel writer and presenter who was awarded a fellowship at the 2023 Wine Writers Symposium in California's Napa Valley. In addition to <i>Decanter</i>, she reviews and writes on wine for a number of publications in Australia and also has a regular wine travel column in <i>International Traveller Magazine</i>. Off the page, she's a television presenter on Channel Nine's <i>Our State on a Plate</i>, a compere at wine functions, and hosts in-person wine and food events throughout Western Australia. Through her company <a href="http://www.earnyourvino.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-saferedirecturl="https://www.google.com/url?q=http://www.earnyourvino.com/&amp;source=gmail&amp;ust=1692187587905000&amp;usg=AOvVaw18WWjWyO-1_cMUF_2ywkRE">Earn Your Vino</a>, Cassandra also delivers immersive wine experiences throughout WA's wine regions.</p></div>

title: Pinot Progress: South American Pinot Noir finds its footing in extreme terroirs
content: <p>Amanda Barnes is an award-winning wine journalist and expert in South American wines and regions. </p><p>Based in Mendoza since 2009 she is a regular South America correspondent, critic and writer for <em>Decanter</em>, as well as other international wine publications, and she is the author and editor of the <em>South America Wine Guide</em>. </p><p>She has been awarded by Born Digital Wine Awards, Millesima Blog Awards, Great Wine Capitals Best Of and Young Wine Writer of the Year. </p><p>She has received a fellowship from the Wine Writers Symposium, a scholarship for the Wine Bloggers Conference, and the Geoffrey Roberts Award. </p>
